why: A is (4_λ) for an abstract Morse.FiltrationHomology: altSum R ≤ altSum of the Morse numbers, and ≤ altSum of the critical-point counts under a cell hypothesis on the slabs. B is (4_λ) for singular homology of a chain ∅ = X_0 ⊆ … ⊆ X_k = X of subsets whose i-th step has homology F in degree λ_i and 0 otherwise, with C_λ = #{i | λ_i = λ}. A ⇒ B: the chain is extended to a monotone ℕ-filtration (RoundTrip.Glue.exists_nat_filtration) and A's morse_inequality is applied to the project's truncatedFiltrationHomology (P = Fin k, step = val, ind = λ). k = 0 (X = ∅) is handled separately. B's alt is the project's altSum verbatim. B ⇒ A fails for lack of content: B concerns only singular homology of cell-like chains, while A holds for any abstract filtration homology and arbitrary slab dimensions.
